key_idea: The central idea is to bound the distance and local testability of quantum and classical LDPC codes by analyzing the 'local minimality' of cycles in a homological chain complex derived from the lifted product of Tanner codes over expander graphs.
reason: This proof achieves a monumental dual breakthrough in classical and quantum coding theory by recasting code properties into the language of algebraic topology. While the required algebraic and structural machinery generates a long chain of technical lemmas, the conceptual framework of chain complexes and local minimality makes the result feel miraculously inevitable.
recognized: Panteleev and Kalachev, Asymptotically Good Quantum and Locally Testable Classical LDPC Codes (2022)
